questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, the hoses should be checked:

options.text: For the right amount of brake fluid.
To make sure they connect to the battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: For leaks.
questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle with power steering, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look especially for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: With an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would with any other braking system. Do not change your braking technique.

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while switching gears:

options.text: You may have trouble putting the vehicle into the next gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble putting the vehicle into the next gear.
questions.explanation: Staying in neutral too long while switching gears may make it hard to shift into the next gear. Do not force it. Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up the engine to match the road speed, and try again.

questions.question: How can you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If it does not return to normal, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the brakes squeak, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times, then press it firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, you may have a leak or another problem.

questions.question: On a slippery road, a driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid passing other vehicles.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Turn gently and do not pass other vehicles unless absolutely necessary.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: A driver who is color blind.
A person who does not know traffic rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: An impaired driver.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who are drunk, tired, on drugs, or sick can be dangerous. Stopping at a green light is one sign that a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: When doing a pre-drive inspection:

options.text: The inspection report is not important.
Review the inspection report only if there will be passengers.
Review the previous inspection report, if there is one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the previous inspection report, if there is one.
questions.explanation: Start the inspection by reviewing the last inspection report. Only sign a new report if any problems noted have been fixed.

questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers.
questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes.
questions.explanation: Before slowing down, lightly tap your brakes. This makes your brake lights flash, warning drivers behind you.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Get some rest.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Continuing to drive is dangerous and can cause a fatal crash. Pep pills may keep you awake briefly, but they won't make you truly alert.

questions.question: If your wheels spin when accelerating on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: If your wheels spin while accelerating on a slippery surface, remove your foot from the accelerator.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: It is caused only by physical distractions.
It increases when you pre-program radio stations.
You can prevent it by avoiding conversations with others while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can prevent it by avoiding conversations with others while driving.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (like reaching for something), mental (like talking to a passenger), or both (like texting). To avoid distracted driving: pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead, avoid difficult conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you leave, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: What is an encroachment?

options.text: A driver misses their scheduled basic skills test.
A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
A driver fails one section of the basic skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the basic skills test. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop within the area of road you can see. Slow down when you cannot see far ahead.

questions.question: Bridges usually freeze:

options.text: Only when temperatures drop well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: When you start an engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Check your gauges when you start the engine. Oil pressure should reach normal level within a few seconds after starting.

questions.question: Heights posted on bridges:
questions.correctAnswerText: Can be incorrect.
questions.explanation: Do not assume posted heights are correct. They may have changed due to road repaving or snow buildup.

questions.question: Using a hands-free phone while driving:

options.text: Only distracts the driver if the driver is speaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can distract the driver.
questions.explanation: Hands-free phones are safer than hand-held phones, but they still distract drivers mentally. Any conversation takes your attention away from driving.

questions.question: Emergency equipment, such as fire extinguishers:

options.text: Is only needed in vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Is only needed for interstate travel.
Is required in all commercial motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required in all commercial motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must carry emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether the road is icy, you should:

options.text: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: Open your window and touch the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on these items, the road is likely icy too.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Ignore the gauges as they are unreliable.
Watch the gauges for signs of trouble.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the gauges for signs of trouble.
questions.explanation: Check your gauges while driving to spot problems early. Before you start driving, make sure all gauges are working properly.
